title: Restricting by a composed restriction in two stages
statement:
Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables, and let $\rho_1, \rho_2$ be two restrictions on those variables, each fixing some coordinates to Boolean values and leaving the rest free. Write $\rho_1 \circ \rho_2$ for their composition, the restriction that on each coordinate uses the value fixed by $\rho_1$ when there is one and otherwise the value assigned by $\rho_2$, and for a restriction $\rho$ write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the function obtained from $f$ by fixing the coordinates set by $\rho$ and evaluating on the remaining free coordinates. Then restricting $f$ by the composition $\rho_1 \circ \rho_2$ gives the same function as first restricting $f$ by $\rho_1$ and then restricting the function $f\!\restriction_{\rho_1}$ by $\rho_2$:
\[
  f\!\restriction_{\rho_1 \circ \rho_2} \;=\; \bigl(f\!\restriction_{\rho_1}\bigr)\!\restriction_{\rho_2}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on Fin n → Bool
ρ₁ is a restriction on n variables
ρ₂ is a restriction on n variables
replaced:
For a Boolean function $f$ and restrictions $\rho_1,\rho_2$, restricting by the composed
restriction equals restricting by $\rho_1$ and then by $\rho_2$:
\[
  \mathrm{restrictFn}\,f\,(\mathrm{composeRestr}\,\rho_1\,\rho_2)
    = \mathrm{restrictFn}\,(\mathrm{restrictFn}\,f\,\rho_1)\,\rho_2.
\]
